processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel blocks were cast via vacuum arc furnace.
Homogenization promotes uniform composition and microstructure throughout the steel blocks.
Homogenized steel is subjected to step-by-step hot rolling reducing thickness to ~11 mm, followed by slow cooling in the oven.

processing_steps.method: water jet cutting machine (OMAX 2626, Kent, Washington, USA)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Samples precisely fabricated to allow accurate geometries and minimize thermal distortion.

Applied TA for S5; 1150 °C is the optimized austenitizing temperature for S1, S2, S4 and S5 where αp is suppressed to negligible levels (S5 residual ≲1 %). Fig. 1(a) prints 'S1, S2, S5: 1150 °C (15 min.)' with heating at 10 K s⁻¹.

processing_steps.method: cooling from austenitization to austempering temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cooling rate sufficiently fast to suppress intermediate phase transformations and ensure fine bainitic transformation.
Complete bainitic transformation observed at 365 °C after 1000 s during austempering; TB = 365 °C is ~34 °C above Ms (331 °C).
After the isothermal bainitic hold the cycle ends with final cooling (Fig. 1 (a)).

structures.overall_structure: Predominantly bainitic microstructure (impingement-free) with film-like retained austenite; slightly coarser bainitic packets at 365 °C with a trace of allotriomorphic ferrite; martensite absent; no SEM-resolvable (Fe,M)xCy precipitates after austempering.

phases_present.morphology: lath/feathery bainite; slightly coarser packets; true lamellar thickness Lt(t) = 55 nm (SD 15 nm)
film-like at bainite lath boundaries (largely film-like).

phases_present.volume_fraction: <1.0 % (αp); trace amount of allotriomorphic ferrite at 365 °C

defects.type: local lattice misorientation / geometrically necessary dislocations (KAM)
defects.lattice_distortion: mean KAM ~0.905°, median 0.789°; phase micro-strain εγ 0.42 %, εα 0.43 %

grain_structure.texture: slightly coarser bainitic packets than at 335 °C; intra-packet orientation clustering with frequent high-angle packet/block boundaries.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: At 365 °C the global KAM field is marginally higher on average than at 335 °C (mean ~0.905° vs 0.825°) but fairly uniform without strongly localised hot-spots; bands of elevated misorientation along lath/packet boundaries.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Moderate Al–C level with small Ni addition promotes very rapid bainitic transformation when austempered slightly above Ms, yielding a predominantly bainitic microstructure with film-like γr and only isolated secondary constituents; TB effectively sets the γr/KAM balance without extensive sheaf impingement or secondary precipitation.
interfaces.interface_notes: In S5 the combination of moderate Al, reduced C and a small Ni addition produces a trace amount of αp, scarce martensite, rapid bainite formation, and a clean interface network; γr is largely film-like at bainite lath boundaries.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: ASTM E8 sub-size round specimens (12.5 mm gauge length, 2.5 mm diameter, 7 mm shoulder length)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile specimens heat-treated using the DIL 805A dilatometer applying the thermal cycle of Fig. 1 (a); sample S5 austempered at T_B 365 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: DIL 805A dilatometer (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE, USA)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Heating at 10 K s⁻¹, cooling at 100 K s⁻¹; cylindrical specimens (Ø5 × 10 mm³)
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine T_A, Ms and bainitic transformation kinetics (Bt) of S5.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Ms = 331 °C for S5; complete bainitic transformation at 365 °C after 1000 s; S5 exhibited the fastest transformation kinetics (Bt 700–1000 s).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany; samples etched with 6 % Nital
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: LOM at 1050 °C benchmark and at selected T_A (1150 °C for S5)
characterization_methods.purpose: Inspect overall ferrite distribution and verify polygonal ferrite (αp) content.
characterization_methods.key_findings: S5 showed prominent αp at 1050 °C and only a very small residual fraction (≲1 %) at 1150 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany; gold sputter coating on etched samples
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SE-SEM imaging of S5 after T_B 335 °C and 365 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal bainite morphology, film-like γr and any precipitates.
characterization_methods.key_findings: 365 °C condition shows an impingement-free structure with film-like γr (arrowed); no SEM-resolvable (Fe,M)xCy after austempering in S5.
EDX used for precipitate chemistry (mainly for S1–S4); no SEM-resolvable precipitates in S5 after austempering.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss SEM equipped with Oxford Instruments EBSD system and software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Accelerating voltage 20 kV, step size 0.2 μm; electropolished/vibratory polished surfaces
characterization_methods.purpose: Assess bainitic packet/grain orientation (IPF) and local misorientation (KAM).
characterization_methods.key_findings: 365 °C: slightly coarser bainitic packets with a trace of allotriomorphic ferrite (F), martensite absent; average KAM 0.905° (median 0.789°).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Malvern Panalytical Empyrean diffractometer (Cu X-ray tube, 40 kV/40 mA, PIXcel 1D detector)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Rietveld refinement of integrated intensities (ASTM E975-13)
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine retained-austenite volume fraction (Vγ) and phase micro-strains (εγ, εα).
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 365 °C Vγ ≈ 26 % with converging phase micro-strains (εγ 0.42 %, εα 0.43 %); no resolvable martensite peaks.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zwick/Roell universal testing machine (250 kN load cell, Zwick Roell Group, Ulm, Germany)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ASTM E8 sub-size round specimens (12.5 mm gauge length, 2.5 mm diameter, 7 mm shoulder length)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure UTS, Rp0.2 and elongation of S5.
characterization_methods.key_findings: S5 at 365 °C: UTS 1315 MPa, El 8.7 % (PSE 11,450 MPa·%).

computational_details.simulation_method: equilibrium phase calculation (standard step calculation method)
computational_details.software_used: MatCalc Version 6.01 (rel 1.003), Institute of Materials Science and Technology, TU Wien, Wien, Austria
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Considered phases: fcc, bcc, liquid, κ-carbide, hcp carbide, AlN, TiCN–TiMoC system
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: For S5 the simulations give a ferrite-free T_A = 986 °C and a carbide-dissolution temperature Tcd = 775 °C (lowest of the five steels).
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: LOM confirms αp suppression in S5 (≲1 % at 1150 °C), consistent with the simulated ferrite-free T_A; 1150 °C selected as the applied T_A.

computational_details.simulation_method: precipitation kinetics TTP simulation (heterogeneous nucleation theory on dislocation and grain-boundary sites, ortho-equilibrium transformation, volumetric misfit considered)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Ti-Mo-C and (Fe,M)xCy carbide systems; κ-carbides treated as fixed phase fractions
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: T_A: 1150 °C, cooling rate 100 K s⁻¹; T_B 365 °C with Bt 1000 s and T_B 335 °C with Bt 700 s (Fig. 8 (d) for S5)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: S5 shows no SEM-resolvable (Fe,M)xCy after austempering, in line with the TTP assessment and the lower alloying level.

unmapped_findings: Sample S5 (TA 1150 °C, TB 365 °C) achieved a product of strength and elongation (PSE) of 11,450 MPa·% (UTS 1315 MPa, El 8.7 %); the overall S5 PSE range across conditions was ≈10.7–11.5 GPa·%.

S5 steel exhibited the fastest bainitic transformation among the studied steels, with an incubation period completed within 10 s and complete bainitic transformation at 365 °C after 1000 s (and at 335 °C after 700 s).
The measured martensite-start temperature of S5 was 331 °C, the highest among the five steels; austempering at 365 °C (~34 °C above Ms) suppresses martensite and promotes bainitic transformation.
The addition of 0.78 wt.% Ni to S5 did not adversely affect the bainitic transformation kinetics and maintained the αp content at a minimal level via its austenite-stabilizing effect.

In S5, (Fe,M)xCy particles precipitate during cooling between approximately 700 °C and 1000 °C according to the TTP simulation; the resulting (Fe,M)xCy and MoC were less present in the final microstructure compared to steels S1–S3.

S5 was positioned, in terms of UTS–El performance, intermediate between steels containing ≈3 wt.% Al and ≈5 wt.% Al (literature alloys with 0.67–0.94 wt.% C): ≈3 wt.% Al alloys gave UTS 1400–2000 MPa and El 9–12 % (PSE ≈12,600–24,000 MPa·%), and ≈5 wt.% Al alloys gave UTS 1300–1850 MPa and El 4–9.5 % (PSE ≈5200–17,575 MPa·%).
MatCalc predicted a 100 K/s cooling-rate TTP diagram for S5 with T_B lines at 365 °C (Bt 1000 s) and 335 °C (Bt 700 s) - the shortest transformation times of the four simulated panels (Fig. 8 (d)).
